column: screen_in_vitro_khatiwara2012.tsv (separate resource, not a column of the compilation)
assay: Tn-seq in S. Typhimurium ATCC 14028; fitness index = output reads / input reads, neutral 1.0, the authors call a gene required at <= 0.2. Four arms: LB 37 C (optimal growth) is the only one used to call in vitro fitness cost; diluted LB, LB + bile acid and LB 42 C are deliberate proxies for host stressors and are carried for audit only. Added because the compilation's graded in vitro column is transferred from S. Typhi, leaving rung 6 resting on one cross-serovar screen; this one is measured in Typhimurium. 110 of the 113 genes in Table S3 transfer to SL1344 one-to-one. The screen analysed 1,931 of ~4,500 genes and published only those crossing threshold, so absence carries no information
citation: Khatiwara A et al. (2012) Appl Environ Microbiol 78:3098

column: screen_in_vitro_canals2019.tsv (separate resource, not a column of the compilation)
assay: TIS in S. Typhimurium ST313 D23580; index = insertion-site density in the output over the input, median-normalised so neutral is 1.0 and a cost is called at <= 0.2, the same five-fold depletion as the ATCC 14028 screen. Three arms: LB 37 C (optimal growth) is the only one used to call in vitro fitness cost; InSPI2 is a SPI-2-inducing minimal medium and the macrophage arm is a host condition, both carried for audit only -- aroA reads 1.18 in LB and 0.05 in InSPI2, so gating on InSPI2 would discard the best-validated attenuated mutants in the literature. The published three-level requirement call is NOT read: it marks 17 of 41 SPI-2 genes required in LB because the input library covers SPI-2 sparsely, whereas on the normalised index 0 of 36 SPI-2 genes reach <= 0.2 in LB and 20 of 36 fall below 0.5 in macrophages. Every gene is reported, not only those crossing threshold, so this is the one in vitro resource whose coverage is genome-wide: 3,998 SL1344 genes receive a value. Transferred from ST313 to SL1344 (ST19) by protein identity (3,459), >=90% identity (400) or unique gene symbol (139)
citation: Canals R et al. (2019) PLoS Pathog 15:e1007948

column: screen_oral_tradis_chaudhuri2013.tsv (separate resource, not a column of the compilation)
assay: Transposon-directed insertion-site sequencing after ORAL challenge; the authors' core set of genes significantly attenuated in all three host species assayed (chicken, pig, cattle). Supplies an attenuation call and the source's own top ordinal category; the paper publishes no per-gene fold change for the core set, so no magnitude is recorded. 591 of the published 611 genes resolve to an SL1344 coding sequence. Added because every other screen here is a systemic mouse infection, in which SPI-1 is largely bypassed
citation: Chaudhuri RR et al. (2013) PLoS Genet 9:e1003456

column: screen_in_vivo_typhi_31447308.tsv (separate resource, not a column of the compilation)
assay: Genome-wide TraDIS of S. Typhi Ty2 in HUMANIZED MICE, the only animal screen here from another serovar and the only one reporting a per-gene FDR. effect_log2 = -logFC, positive = depleted in the animal; attenuation is called at the authors' own q <= 0.05, not retuned. Controls pass cleanly: 0 of the 44 assayed ribosomal proteins are called, and the complete 10-gene Vi antigen locus is recovered. 74 of 4,589 genes are significant (1.6%). Transferred to SL1344 by identical protein accession, unique gene symbol, or a single >=90% identity match: 3,034 of 4,868 genes (62.3%) receive a value and 47 of the 74 significant genes transfer. The 27 that do not are mostly structures Typhimurium does not share -- the Vi locus, 5 O-antigen rfb and 4 waa outer-core genes. Absence of a value is NOT evidence of no phenotype. Not used to license an in vitro dispensable call, because the viable mutant existed in Typhi
citation: Nickerson KP et al. (2019) Cell Host Microbe 26:245-258

assay: Genome-wide screen for genes required for long-term systemic infection of Nramp1-positive mice

Microarray-based negative selection of a signature-tagged transposon mutant library in RAW 264.7 macrophages and in the spleens of BALB/cJ mice. The column name is a misnomer carried from the source workbook: the senior author is Falkow but the first author is Chan, and the assay is a genome-wide negative-selection screen, not a targeted one. It is the THINNEST input in this table at 18 genes (0.4% of the genome), so it is carried for its direction rather than its coverage
citation: Chan K, Kim CC, Falkow S (2005) Infect Immun 73:5438
